open_points.subject: FlowActivation (M18) creation / activate flow action
open_points.text: K-08: "A read-only flow is activated by the kernel once proven" vs Primary actions: "activate a flow | agent or owner asks; the kernel activates a proven read-only version at once"
open_points.question: For a proven read-only flow version, is FlowActivation created automatically at prove time, or only when someone calls activate?
options: Both paths allowed (idempotent if already active)
open_points.default_guess: Automatic on successful proof, with activate returning the existing active version.

open_points.subject: Effect authority rules (approval vs standing grant)
open_points.text: K-08: "The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key and never repeats an effect without a fresh approval." and decision 18 addendum: "A difference voids the approval, not a standing grant: where the owner's active grant covers the node, the send goes under the grant without asking."
open_points.question: When an effect is being sent again (or re-sent with changed built request) and a standing grant is active, does the grant authorize the send without fresh approval, or is fresh approval always required for repeats?
options: Fresh approval always required for any repeat
Standing grant may authorize repeats except the explicit not_applied case
Standing grant always overrides approval freshness rules
open_points.default_guess: Standing grant authorizes unless the prior outcome was resolved not_applied, which always needs fresh approval.

open_points.subject: Implementation (M05) read exposure to agents
open_points.text: Primary actions: "inspect functions ... | owner, agent | typed description" and K-12: "For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation ...; for composition, contracts, bindings and not implementation bodies."
open_points.question: Can an agent read implementation code via inspect outside the repair context, and if so under what scope?
options: No: inspect for agents never includes implementation bodies
Yes: any agent may inspect implementation bodies
Only the slot targeted for repair is readable as code to the agent
open_points.default_guess: Only the repair-target slot’s implementation body is returned to an agent; general inspect omits bodies.
